solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Gibe by our CO at waxed garment

parts.note: a gibe is a barb, a cutting remark
taken as written
taken as written, the abbreviation for commanding officer
taken as written

explanation.surface: A jeer aimed at the commanding officer about his oiled outdoor jacket.
explanation.walkthrough: A BARBOUR is a British brand of waxed cotton jacket, the classic country coat.
explanation.definitionFit: The brand's signature product is a waterproof jacket treated with wax, so the description names it by its finish.

clue.text: Unconventional spa/hydro abroad — 16, 17 includes it

parts.note: bohemian describes an artistic, free-living, unconventional manner

indicators.note: abroad in its sense of astray or all over the place tells us to rearrange these letters

explanation.surface: An odd foreign health resort, said to feature in the linked entries.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on 16 and 17 down, the Queen album A Night at the Opera, which includes this song.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous Queen single appears as a track on that 1975 album, so the album contains it.

clue.text: See 1
Ring from abroad about coming over

parts.note: someone abroad is out of the country

indicators.note: in a down clue coming over says this little word is flipped end to end

parts.note: re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A ring of people from overseas who are visiting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' is a link word. On an archery target the outer is the ring furthest from the bull.
explanation.definitionFit: The outermost circle on a target is called by this name, a hit there scoring least.

clue.text: Put back on site

parts.note: re as a preposition means on the subject of
a site is a place or location

explanation.surface: Someone told to reinstall something on location.
explanation.definitionFit: To put something back where it was is to restore it to its position, a direct synonym.

clue.text: In forest, Estonian, he killed his mother and her lover

definitions.text: he killed his mother and her lover

indicators.note: in says the answer sits inside the run of letters of these words

explanation.surface: A murder story set in an Estonian woodland.
explanation.walkthrough: In Greek myth this son of Agamemnon killed Clytemnestra and Aegisthus to avenge his father.
explanation.definitionFit: Greek legend tells of the son who avenged his father by slaying Clytemnestra and her paramour Aegisthus.

clue.text: Finest fruit for figurehead?

parts.note: top means best or finest, as in top quality
a banana is a fruit

explanation.surface: Choosing the best fruit to put on a ship's prow, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link word. The question mark flags that figurehead here means a leader, not a ship's carving.
explanation.definitionFit: The informal phrase means the most important person, the boss or nominal leader of a group.

clue.text: Philip, a star

definitions.meaning: a short form of that boy's name, as in Great Expectations
a star worn on an army officer's shoulder to show rank

explanation.definitionFit: The short name is a familiar diminutive of the boy's name, and the rank badge on a uniform is so called.

clue.text: Well-liked, but not posh, district of London

indicators.note: not here means take away the posh letter from the longer word

parts.note: someone well-liked is popular
U is the old label for upper-class or posh usage

explanation.surface: A London neighbourhood liked by many but lacking airs.
explanation.walkthrough: POPLAR is an area of East London.
explanation.definitionFit: The district lies in Tower Hamlets in the East End, named after the trees once grown there.

clue.text: A padre organised procession

indicators.note: organised means arranged, so these letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A priest arranged a march.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal march of people through the streets is a procession, a simple synonym.

clue.text: Listen to trombone at first, then organ

parts.note: to listen to is to hear

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of trombone

explanation.surface: Hearing the trombone first and then the church organ at a concert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'then' is a link word. Organ looks musical but means a body part.
explanation.definitionFit: The muscle that pumps blood is one of the body's main organs.

clue.text: One who lured Greek character right across Dieppe, slyly

indicators.note: across says the two outer pieces span the jumbled port name

parts.note: pi is a letter of the Greek alphabet

indicators.note: slyly suggests a crafty rearrangement of the letters of Dieppe

explanation.surface: A Greek right-winger sneaking across a French port.
explanation.walkthrough: The Greek letter and the R form the outside, with the port's letters scrambled between them. 'One who lured' refers to the Hamelin legend, not a seducer.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Hamelin legend the musician lured first the rats and then the town's children away.

clue.text: Reprobate tortured miner's cat

indicators.note: tortured means twisted out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A villain who tormented a mineworker's pet.
explanation.definitionFit: A reprobate is an unprincipled scoundrel, and a miscreant is a wrongdoer of the same kind.

clue.text: A flipping 28 may help one to get a prize

indicators.note: flipping means turning over, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: 28 across is a tie, and a tie in sport is a draw

explanation.surface: A tie in a match turned over might help win a trophy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may help one to get' is link material. 'flipping' turns DRAW into WARD.
explanation.definitionFit: An award is something given as a prize or honour for achievement.

clue.text: Musical instruction given in article by eminent Florentine

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
the poet Dante Alighieri was born in Florence

explanation.surface: A music direction attributed to a famous man of Florence.
explanation.definitionFit: Composers write this Italian tempo marking to ask for a moderately slow, walking pace.

clue.text: Moving into Chile, about when stone weapons prevailed

indicators.note: moving means shifting position, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Relocating to Chile in the era of stone weapons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is a link word, meaning concerning the period.
explanation.definitionFit: The New Stone Age was the period when polished stone tools and weapons were in use.

clue.text: See 27
Film giant, Hope, that era tranformed

indicators.note: transformed, printed with a slip, means changed into another shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A huge film star, Bob Hope perhaps, changed that period of cinema.
explanation.walkthrough: The 1935 Marx Brothers comedy, also the title of a Queen album. Hope suggests the comedian, but it is just fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1935 Marx Brothers picture is a famous comedy film.

clue.text: See 16
Bench in favour of mercy, initially

parts.note: for means in support of

indicators.note: initially picks the opening letter of mercy

explanation.surface: Judges on the bench leaning towards mercy at first.
explanation.walkthrough: Bench looks like the judiciary but means a long seat; a form is an old word for a backless bench.
explanation.definitionFit: A form is a long backless seat, as in old school rooms, so it is a kind of bench.

clue.text: A small amount of some poetry penned by mother

indicators.note: penned by means enclosed by, so the poetry word goes inside the mother word

parts.note: mum is an informal word for mother
odic means relating to an ode, a kind of poem

explanation.surface: A few lines of verse written by a parent.
explanation.definitionFit: A modicum is a small quantity of something, as in a modicum of sense.

clue.text: Sound check

definitions.meaning: sound as in firm and loyal, a steadfast supporter
check as in stop the flow of blood from a wound

explanation.definitionFit: The word means loyal and firm, and as a verb (also spelt stanch) it means to stop a flow.

clue.text: Awful massacre mostly brings contempt

indicators.note: awful suggests something badly made, so these letters are rearranged
mostly says to use most of the word, dropping its last letter

explanation.surface: A dreadful slaughter provokes scorn.
explanation.definitionFit: Sarcasm is mocking, scornful language, an expression of contempt.

clue.text: Bird — adult one disappearing from view over top of trees

parts.note: A is the film certificate for adult

indicators.note: disappearing from says the letter for one is taken out of the view word

parts.note: a voice is an opinion or view, as in having a voice
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: top of picks the first letter of trees, at the top in a down answer

explanation.surface: A bird watcher's adult companion vanishing out of sight above the treetops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' is a link word: in a down answer the earlier pieces lie over the T.
explanation.definitionFit: The avocet is a black-and-white wading bird with an upturned bill, emblem of the RSPB.

clue.text: Greek leisure film

parts.note: ease means rest or leisure

explanation.surface: A Greek film about relaxing.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1978 musical starring John Travolta and Olivia Newton-John is a well-known film.

clue.text: Composer from Hanover died

indicators.note: from says the answer is taken out of the run of letters in these words

explanation.surface: A composer from the German city of Hanover has died.
explanation.definitionFit: Giuseppe Verdi was the Italian composer of operas such as Aida and La Traviata.

clue.text: Slipping up, likewise, going after diamonds in act of boldness

indicators.note: going after says these pieces follow the suit letter

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for the card suit diamonds
slipping up means making mistakes, erring
do, short for ditto, means the same again

explanation.surface: Making blunders, while following a girl with jewels, takes nerve.
explanation.definitionFit: Derring-do is daring, heroic action, the stuff of adventure stories.

clue.text: Completely at home with everyone

parts.note: someone at home is in
all means everyone

explanation.surface: Being entirely at ease with all people.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means altogether or in total, as in fifty in all, close to completely.

clue.text: Short talk about a church tea dance

indicators.note: short means the word is cut, losing its final letter

parts.note: a chat is a talk
cha (or char) is slang for tea

explanation.surface: A brief chat at a church tea party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' cuts the last letter of the talk word; 'about' wraps the church abbreviation round A. Each of the three pieces gives the same three letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The cha-cha-cha is a lively Latin American ballroom dance.

clue.text: Clarinettist awaits her arrangement

indicators.note: an arrangement in music or otherwise is a reordering, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A clarinet player waits for her new musical arrangement.
explanation.walkthrough: Artie Shaw was an American swing-era clarinettist and bandleader.
explanation.definitionFit: Artie Shaw led one of the big bands of the 1930s and was celebrated for his clarinet playing.

clue.text: Note about one's obligation

indicators.note: about says the note goes round the numeral

parts.note: te is a note in the sol-fa scale
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A memo concerning a person's duty.
explanation.definitionFit: A tie is a bond or commitment that restricts you, as in family ties.

clue.text: Unexpectedly, Eliot came round in the morning for a drink

indicators.note: round says the jumbled letters go around the morning abbreviation
unexpectedly suggests things turning out differently, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: a.m. stands for ante meridiem, in the morning

explanation.surface: T. S. Eliot surprisingly dropped by one morning for a soothing drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unexpectedly' makes COMILETEA from ELIOT CAME; 'round' puts AM inside it after the C.
explanation.definitionFit: A herbal infusion of chamomile flowers, taken as a soothing beverage.
